lead.purpose: Row titles, lead text, primary buttons on a phone, the value in a field.

body.purpose: Body copy and list rows; prose caps at 68ch.

caption.purpose: Metadata; the floor for a figure or a rating.

micro.purpose: The floor for any functional text: badges, counts, captions on a pin.

shadows.name: elev-1
shadows.purpose: A resting object with no border: an icon button on a photo, the selected segment.

shadows.name: elev-2
shadows.purpose: Raised: a popover, a sticky bar over content.

shadows.name: elev-3
shadows.purpose: Overlay: a sheet or a dialog.

motion.name: dur-1
motion.purpose: Immediate feedback: a press, a chip toggling, a hover tint.

motion.name: dur-2
motion.purpose: A routine state change and every exit.

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: A surface arriving: a sheet, a dialog, a popover.

motion.name: dur-4
motion.purpose: One authored movement over distance: the map camera, one leg of the route reveal.

narrative.overview:
Carta is a travel app you want to open: photos sell the place, and one calm price line with its source tells the truth under every photo. The look is "Lagoon" (T419, owner decision 2026-10-13): the category standard of Airbnb, Polarsteps and Wanderlog, executed at their craft level rather than reinvented. White surfaces sit on a warm light grey; ink is a blue-grey that is never black; one deep lagoon teal carries every action and every selection; sun yellow marks best value and nothing else; one friendly typeface, Figtree, sets everything, figures included, with tabular numerals.

The density is a working app, not a brochure. Explore and Destinations default to compact rows, about ten to a phone screen, each a small rounded photo, a name, a rating and a price line such as "€49 a day" with its source word. Large photo tiles appear on rails and the home page, where inspiration leads. Depth is quiet: objects at rest carry a hairline border, and only what floats (a sheet, a popover, a control over a photograph) takes a soft ink shadow.

The world refuses two things, both confirmed by the owner in the direction contract (`continent-app/.impeccable/surfaces/continent-app.md`): the brochure hero with text laid over a photograph, and the dark instrument look of black slabs and dark selected states.
keyCharacteristics: Photography leads; text never sits on a photograph.
One teal for everything that acts or is selected, as a light tint plus teal text, never a dark slab.
Every colour outside the neutrals and teal has exactly one job.
One typeface, tabular figures everywhere, so prices line up and settle in place.
Borders at rest, shadows only on what floats.
Every control is 44 px on touch, with a 2 px teal focus ring.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal means it acts or it is selected. Nothing decorative, no rating, no gem and no status is ever teal.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Ochre is a rating, plum a hidden gem, sun yellow best value, red destruction. A colour borrowed for a second job stops meaning the first.

rules.name: The No Slab Rule
rules.body: A selected state is the light teal tint with a teal label and a mark (a tick, an underline, a lifted thumb). Never a dark fill, so the app never reads as black.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing functional is set under 11 px, and no figure or rating under 12 px. T421 raised every rule that was under 10 px; the older per-screen files still hold px sizes from 10 px up, which the migration moves onto the scale.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every column of figures uses tabular numerals in the one family. A figure that changes updates in place, never with a count-up.

rules.name: The Compact Default Rule
rules.body: Lists where places are compared default to compact rows (about ten to a phone screen); large photo tiles belong to rails and the home page.

rules.name: The Border Or Shadow Rule
rules.body: Elevation is declared once per object: a border or a shadow, never both.

dos: **Do** read a role (`--action`, `--surface`, `--text-3`) in every new or touched rule, and build from the kit in `src/components/ui/`.
**Do** keep one primary Button per view; everything else is secondary or quiet.
**Do** show selection as `--select-bg` with `--select-ink` and a mark: a tick on a chip, an underline on a tab, a lifted thumb on a segment.
**Do** put a caption under a photograph, never on it.
**Do** give every control a 44 px (`--tap`) target on touch and the 2 px `--focus` ring on `:focus-visible`.
**Do** print every euro through `formatMoney()` or `<Money>`: whole euros where places are compared, cents on receipts and totals, `~€87 est.` for an estimate.
**Do** declare elevation once: a `--border` at rest, or an `--elev-*` shadow on what floats.
**Do** take every duration and easing from the motion tokens and give every transition a reduced-motion branch.
donts: **Don't** paint a selected state as a dark fill; the dark slab is the look Lagoon refused.
**Don't** use teal for anything that does not act or is not selected, or ochre, plum, sun yellow or red outside their one job.
**Don't** set sun yellow as text; use `--best-ink`.
**Don't** add a gradient, a second typeface, a monospaced face for figures, or a hex outside `01-tokens.css` and the token mirror.
**Don't** set functional text under 11 px, or a figure or rating under 12 px.
**Don't** give one object both a border and a shadow.
**Don't** write a euro sign into an i18n string, call `toFixed` on a price, or round a figure on a receipt.
**Don't** use a placeholder as the only name of a field.
**Don't** write em dashes, en dashes, middots or bullet characters as separators in any copy.
